## Crash-safe TinyDB JSONStorage writes (2026-11-03)

The owner asked for crash-safe JSONStorage writes after a service was OOM-killed mid-write. The kill left a truncated db.json that TinyDB could no longer open. The ask came in at 04:25 UTC on 2026-11-03.

The only recorded work is an exploration of tinydb/storages.py (observation #1), done within seconds of the ask. It found that JSONStorage keeps a long-lived r+ file handle and has no atomic write path. A process that dies mid-write can therefore leave a partial file.

Memory holds no implementation, PR, test or release for this request. It is early-stage, with the problem understood and no fix built.

## What this teaches so far

There is too little history to draw conclusions about stalls, rework or turnaround. The next chapter depends on whether the fix is built and merged. A likely approach is a write to a temporary file followed by an atomic rename. That is an expectation, not something recorded in memory.
